programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: The Roma live in most countries, but do not have their own country.According to estimates, there are from 8 to 15 million of them in the world, and in Romania - from about 500,000 to 2 million.Among the many Roma communities, we can mention the Gabors, who traditionally have the same surname to honor the Hungarian king from whom they received rights in the 17th century.They are referred to as aristocracy due to their light skin and financial status.They are distinguished by their attachment to tradition and the Adventist church.Men wear hats and mustaches.If they do not have the latter, it means that they have renounced their origins.Women, on the other hand, must hide their hair from marriage until death, and cannot wear makeup, lipstick or long nails.Their beauty lies in their naturalness.Although individual families traditionally pursue specific professions, they run the home.Martyna Wojciechowska, however, meets Rosalina in Transylvania, who is learning crafts in her future father-in-law's workshop.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Saudi Arabia is one of the few absolute monarchies in the world where Muslim Sharia law still applies.Raha Moharrak was born there - she had enough courage and determination to break the prevailing patterns, thanks to which she was able to fulfill her dreams and conquer the Crown of the Earth, the highest peaks of seven continents.The heroine of the episode achieved this as the first woman from Saudi Arabia.In a country where her gender gained voting rights only in 2011, and in 2018 they were allowed to drive a car or travel abroad without the consent of a male guardian.The biggest problem for Raha was getting her father's consent to participate in the Kilimanjaro expedition, because according to Sharia law, a daughter must obey her parent, and he was against her idea, as was traditional society.However, the girl did not give up.When she conquered Mount Everest, she became a national media star.She continues to inspire other women.

programme.title: Man vs World

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Malawi is a small East African country.Martyna Wojciechowska visits Theresa Kachindamoto, who lives and works in the Dedza district.She is called the Terminator by the inhabitants of the country.She was born into a tribal royal family, the youngest of thirteen siblings.When her eldest brother died, the rest of her siblings elected her as the leader of the almost million-strong community.Never before has a woman performed such an important function.Thanks to her rule, Theresa gained fame and notoriety.During the dozen or so years she was in power, she opposed the customs of the time, annulling over five thousand marriages of underage girls.However, the activities of the heroine of the episode are appreciated not only in her country.At the White House, she received the Local Community Leader award from Michelle Obama and Hillary Clinton.Thanks to Chief Kachindamoto, thousands of underage women were able to return to school - previously 40% of them were married off before they turned 18.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: In Georgia, there is a clear division into female and male roles.Women have to take care of the house and give birth to children, while men work.In the Caucasus, family is the most valuable, infertility is a taboo topic.Mariam Kukunashvili helps couples, including homosexual ones, who want to have children but are struggling with difficulties.She created a network of clinics, and today she is one of the most influential and richest women in the country.She was inspired by her own story - to become a mother, she underwent many years of treatment, struggled with difficult experiences, and finally used the help of surrogates.Patients can benefit from in vitro treatment, the services of surrogate mothers or an egg bank.Similar practices are a controversial topic in Georgia, especially among women.Mariam Kukunashvili breaks stereotypes in the context of traditional society.Its activities have expanded to other parts of the world, including:Ukraine, South Africa, Mexico and Kenya.Thanks to this, 7,000 children from 70 countries have already been born.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Kenya, located in East Africa, is inhabited by 55 million people, over 40 different tribes who speak almost 70 languages ​​in total.Although there is a real mosaic of cultures and beliefs there, not everyone is accepted, and being different can even cost your life.Martyna Wojciechowska visits this republic to meet Darlan.She claims to be the first outed intersex person in her country.Today, he is popular, sings, records music videos, designs clothes, and preaches tolerance.However, this was not always the case.A child born with sexual organs different from those typical of a boy or girl may be considered a curse on the community and killed.Darlan's childhood was marked by humiliation, sarcastic remarks, but also attacks and loneliness.Currently he is fighting for "others".The Darlan Rukih Church is one of the 4,000 officially registered in Kenya and has half a million believers.He cares for all those who are rejected.

programme.title: The Extraordinary States of Procopius
programme.desc: Marcin Prokop will go on a spontaneous journey around America in a program full of humor.During his journey across the United States, which lasts over a month, the journalist will cover thousands of kilometers.Viewers will have the opportunity to see the alleys of the largest Chinese district in the US, find themselves behind the walls of the most famous prison, Alcatraz, and look out the window of the tallest skyscraper in San Francisco.The host will stop at the world's largest stop for giant trucks, visit a hippie town and visit a unique restaurant connected to a laundry.The audience will be able to feast their eyes on amazing landscapes, unique national parks and wonderful waterfalls In this episode, Marcin will go to San Francisco.The presenter will cross the Golden Gate Bridge, where Agent 007 fought a murderous fight with Max Zorin in the film about the adventures of James Bond.He will also visit the colorful Castro district, where Harvey Milk once fought for homosexual rights.Then he will go to the Haight-Ashbury district, the cradle of hippies, where Marcin will undergo a surprising metamorphosis.A visit to this city would not be complete without a trip to Lombard Street, known as the most twisted street in the world.After a walk through the city streets, the presenter will take us to the most liberal beach in California and show us the famous Alcatraz prison, where Al Capone ended his gangster career.
